learningObjectives: Connect interface screens into interactive user flows.
Use triggers and actions to simulate common interactions.
Create prototypes that communicate intended user behavior.
Select transitions that support rather than distract from the user task.

activities.title: Prototype Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the main parts of an interactive prototype.

content.concept: A prototype connects screens through triggers, actions, transitions, and destinations to simulate an experience.
content.tip: Explore each part and identify how it contributes to an interaction flow.

descriptions: The event that starts an interaction.
The behavior performed after the trigger.
The screen or state reached by the interaction.
The visual change between states or screens.
The complete sequence of interactions that supports a user task.

activities.title: Trigger and Action Matcher
activities.instruction: Match each trigger with the appropriate prototype action.

content.concept: Triggers such as clicks, taps, hovering, dragging, and keyboard actions can initiate prototype responses.
content.tip: Choose an action that logically follows the user's interaction.

choices: Tap button → Navigate to another screen
config.answer: Tap button → Navigate to another screen

activities.title: Prototype Flow Builder
activities.instruction: Arrange the screens to complete a simple user journey.

content.concept: Prototype flows model how users move between screens while completing a specific task.
content.tip: Follow the user's goal from entry point to successful completion.

activities.title: Transition Matcher
activities.instruction: Choose a transition that best fits each interaction.

content.concept: Transitions should reinforce the relationship between states without distracting users from their task.
content.tip: Prefer transitions that communicate continuity and maintain a clear sense of context.

choices: Button to new screen → Instant or subtle dissolve
Opening a side panel → Slide in
Expanding an object into details → Smart transition
config.answer: Opening a side panel → Slide in
